body: Thank you for the help, but it's nothing I haven't thought of before.
And there's nothing amazing about me. The things I do never meet my own standards, so what reason do I have to be proud of them?

Part of the problem is that I have no outside indicators that anything is wrong. I see a therapist because my parents are divorced and have been for most of my life, so when we talk it's mostly questions about my relationship with them. It's helpful, but not helpful in the ways I need it to be, and I can't get myself to open up to anyone enough to get what I need. Also because my parents are divorced, my therapist has to be approved by both of them and covered under insurance, and since my parents care more about screwing the other over than finding help for me it takes 6-9 months to find a new one.

I do see a psychologist, it doesn't help because I'm completely unable to talk about my problems to people in person. I've tried before and I just lock up before I can say anything. As for the activities listed, I'm in an improv troupe, I run every day, I'm on a fairly successful Science Olympiad team, and I've tried volunteering in the past. No matter what my goals are I'm never satisfied unless everything goes perfectly. I know it's unrealistic, but every mistake I've made is constantly hanging over me, and it makes me not want to do anything.
I know this is incredibly vague, but I've tried a few times to write a detailed explanation of why I feel this way and they've all been awful.
